# kubernetes_gateway_class_v1

Manages a cluster-scoped Gateway API v1 GatewayClass. Requires preinstalled Gateway API CRDs. Creation does not wait for controller acceptance.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `metadata` (Block List) Standard GatewayClass's metadata. Exactly one metadata block is required. More info: https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#metadata (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--metadata))
- `spec` (Block List) Desired GatewayClass configuration. Exactly one block is required. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--spec))
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Cluster-scoped GatewayClass name.
- `status` (Object) Controller-reported conditions and supported_features. Conditions include type, status, reason, message, observed_generation and last_transition_time. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--status))

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "kubernetes_gateway_class_v1" "example" {
  metadata {
    name = "example"
  }

  spec {
    controller_name = "example.com/gateway-controller"
    description     = "Example GatewayClass"
  }
}
```

Set `controller_name` to the identifier documented by your Gateway controller.
Kubernetes stores a class with any well-formed identifier, but only a matching
controller accepts it.

### Controller parameters

```terraform
resource "kubernetes_gateway_class_v1" "internal" {
  metadata {
    name = "internal"
  }

  spec {
    controller_name = "example.com/gateway-controller"
    description     = "Gateways for internal traffic"

    parameters_ref {
      group     = "example.com"
      kind      = "GatewayConfig"
      name      = "internal"
      namespace = "gateway-system"
    }
  }
}
```

`parameters_ref` points to a controller-specific configuration object. Use the
`group` and `kind` documented by your controller, `group = ""` for the core API
group, and `namespace` only for a namespaced referent. Manage the referenced
object separately; the provider neither creates it nor validates its contents.

## Prerequisites

Install the Gateway API CRDs before using this resource. The provider does not
install CRDs or a Gateway controller. The schema targets the Gateway API v1.6.3
Standard channel. Credentials need permission to manage cluster-scoped
GatewayClasses and to read API discovery, which the provider uses to tell a
missing GatewayClass from missing CRDs.

## Behavior notes

- **Controller acceptance:** Creation succeeds once Kubernetes stores the object.
  It does not wait for the controller to accept the class, and it does not
  provision a Gateway or load balancer. Inspect `status` for the controller's
  response. A condition whose `observed_generation` is older than
  `metadata[0].generation` does not describe the latest spec.
- **Replacement:** Changing `metadata[0].name`, `metadata[0].generate_name`, or
  `spec[0].controller_name` replaces the GatewayClass. Refer to your controller's
  documentation for how other class changes affect existing Gateways.
- **Cluster scope:** GatewayClass has no namespace. Set either `metadata[0].name`
  or `metadata[0].generate_name`.

## Timeouts

`kubernetes_gateway_class_v1` provides the following [Timeouts](/docs/configuration/resources.html#timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default `10 minutes`
- `read` - Default `10 minutes`
- `update` - Default `10 minutes`
- `delete` - Default `10 minutes`

Deletion waits until the GatewayClass is gone. While Gateways use the class, the
controller may keep the `gateway-exists-finalizer.gateway.networking.k8s.io`
finalizer, so delete dependent Gateways before their class. The provider never
removes finalizers. A replacement that keeps the same name cannot use
`create_before_destroy`.

## Import

GatewayClass can be imported using its name, without a namespace, e.g.

```
$ terraform import kubernetes_gateway_class_v1.example example
```

Identity imports use `api_version = "gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1"`,
`kind = "GatewayClass"`, and `name`. An identity with a different `kind` or
`api_version` is rejected.
